newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebel leader Kabila says Zairean offensive blocked.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader Kabila says Zairean offensive blocked.

text.p: Rebel leader Laurent Kabilia said on Friday his army had checked a counter-offensive by mercenary-backed government forces against the strip of eastern Zaire seized by his soldiers last year.

"In the south, toward Shaba, it's all over. In Kisangani province, everything is going well, we have stopped the famous counter-offensive which we have totally wiped out," Kabila said in an interview broadcast on Radio France Internationale from Goma, eastern Zaire.
"We control the territory...In the last two days there have been no more battles. We have discovered that the enemy has retreated considerably due to the losses," the rebel leader said.
Kabila's claims could not immediately be verified.
But government and military sources said in Kinshasa on Thursday that the Zairean counter-offensive had run into resistance on several fronts.
The accounts from Kinshasa were in line with reports from Rwanda that rebels in eastern Zaire were pushing south and west, opening new fronts to frustrate the army's counter-offensive.
Kabila said he had beefed up his forces with 8,000 new recruits while there had been 2,363 government soldiers killed.

Asked what were his military objectives, he said he had no designs on the government stronghold of Kisangani, which has a crucial airfield and has been used by government forces as a staging point for the counter-offensive.
"We want these gentlemen to come and sit down at a negotiating table rather than go back to their wily old ways," he said.

Kabila also flatly denied allegations that he was being aided by troops from Rwanda or Uganda, saying he had all the soldiers, arms, transport vehicles and petrol he needed from the areas he had "liberated."

"We get (our equipment) by taking it from the bodies of dead soldiers. And then there are plenty of soldiers who give themselves up. Did you know that 5,600 Zairean soldiers have come over to our side along with their weapons?"

"The lorries you saw were commercial vehicles -- people have to make a living. There are nine million people living in the territory which we occupy," he said. "I swear to you that I have no outside aid."
However, Kabila later stated that weapons were sometimes purchased from munitions firms and smuggled into eastern Zaire through neighbouring countries.
Zaire's ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and his government launched its counter-offensive on January 20 after losing a long strip of eastern territory to Kabila's rebels late last year.
Mobutu was in southern France at the time, resting after cancer treatment at his palatial villa in the Riviera town of Roquebrune-Cap-Martin.
